jobs.prompt: Merge-queue bottleneck seen on atlas-seafloor: the integration lock is repo-wide, so an integrate or merge in one worktree blocks another worktree that targets a different branch. tools/integration-lock.mjs acquireIntegrationLock takes two locks: a machine-wide one under the live directory named integrate-KEY where KEY is a hash of repoKey(root) (the identity shared by every worktree of the repository) and a per-root one at .swarm/integration.lock. Callers: tools/swarm.mjs (line ~1462) and tools/swarm/core-71.mjs (line ~199). Change: (1) the machine-wide lock becomes PER TARGET BRANCH: acquireIntegrationLock(root, { runId, branch, ... }) resolves the branch the integration commits to (the branch checked out in root, read with git symbolic-ref --short HEAD without a shell; an explicit branch option wins; a detached HEAD uses a per-worktree key made from the real path of root so detached worktrees never block each other) and the lock key hashes repoKey plus a separator plus the branch name; two worktrees on different branches no longer block each other, two integrates targeting the same branch still serialize, and the error message names the branch (integrate-locked: another integrate holds branch BRANCH of this repository (pid, run, root, started)). The per-root lock stays as it is (it is already per worktree). Stale-lock handling, owner.json, release order and warnings stay exactly as they are. (2) Shared files: find every write that goes to a file shared by all worktrees of the repository (a path resolved against the main worktree or the git common directory instead of the current root, for example the main checkout ledger and state files, the usage ledger, the merge queue journal, the shared tickets and registry files; read how each writer finds its file) and protect each such write with a SHORT repo-wide lock: a new function withSharedWriteLock(root, name, fn, { maxHoldMs = 5000, staleMs = 30000 }) in tools/integration-lock.mjs (mkdir-based like the existing locks, key from repoKey and the file name, owner.json with pid and host, stale after staleMs when the pid is dead or the age exceeds it, waits with short polls up to 10 seconds then fails with a clear message naming the file); the long integrate lock must never be held while waiting for a shared-file lock for longer than needed, and a shared write holds its lock only for the read-modify-write itself (no checks, no model calls, no git operations inside); log a warning line when a shared lock was held longer than maxHoldMs. Do not change any other behavior. Do not statically import install.mjs. Keep every existing test passing (the integration lock tests and all integrate and queue tests). Tests in tests/integration-lock-branch.test.mjs, hermetic (temp git repo with two worktrees created with git worktree add on branches a and b, temp live directory, injected pid checks, no ambient environment): two acquires from worktrees on branches a and b both succeed at the same time; two acquires on the same branch: the second fails with the message naming the branch; after release the second succeeds; a detached worktree does not block a branch worktree or another detached worktree; stale lock cleanup per branch still works; the explicit branch option wins; withSharedWriteLock serializes two concurrent writers of the same file name (a counter proves no lost update), lets writers of different names run in parallel, clears a stale lock, times out with the message naming the file, and warns when held too long; a regression test that the old repo-wide key no longer blocks (the live directory contains one lock directory per branch). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: tests that reference these files in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge.

Hand-build commit windows expire after 2 hours and the owner has to re-approve each one. Commit windows are hand-build requests that carry --git commit,push for a list of files (swarm handbuild request --kind KIND --reason R --files F1,F2 --git commit,push --minutes N). Standing approval from the owner: under the policy engine, commit windows for SWARM-GENERATED files in a worktree on a non-protected branch are approved automatically and logged. The owner approves only real hand-built code. Add a conditional standing rule to the default rules in tools/policy.mjs (id commit-window-generated), kind hand-build-request (check how the existing hand-build rules and the elevated git check gitFactsOk and isHandbuildItem identify the kind; keep their fail-closed behavior): auto-approve when ALL of these facts are exactly true: git operations requested are a subset of commit and push (no force, no delete, no reset, no checkout of other branches, no merge, no tag); the branch fact is a plain trimmed non-empty string that is not protected (not main, master, a release branch, HEAD, or any remote form, same normalization as the existing protectedBranch helper); every listed file is a swarm-generated path: docs/scope/ (scope files, build plan, context, waves), coordination/manifests/, coordination/handoff/, coordination/HANDOFF.md, coordination/TASK.md, coordination/review/ (never committed but allowed in a window), docs/state/, .swarm/project/ ledger files (tickets.json, tickets.log, backlog.json, scope.snapshot.md) and docs/plans/ideas.md is NOT included; paths are normalized (no .. segments, no absolute paths, no symlink escapes, case-sensitive prefixes) and an empty file list means the owner; the request is not elevated (kind other than secret, emergency, swarm-cannot do not matter for this rule: the rule keys on the files and git operations, but a request for source, tests, config, workflows, package files or any path outside the list always needs the owner, even when mixed with generated files: ONE non-generated file makes the whole request owner-only). Window length: the approval lasts min(requested minutes, 120) and is logged with the rule id, the files, the branch and the expiry in the existing auto-decision log (log before apply, as the engine already does) and in the hand-build action log; a new request for the same files while a window is still open extends nothing and simply succeeds again (the policy pass approves each request as it arrives, so the orchestrator is never blocked for the owner). The approval record created is the same one swarm handbuild approve creates for the request (same expiry semantics) so the guard allows the commit; the guard still enforces everything else (staged content hashes, protected branches). Wire: make sure runPolicyPass (called by the autopilot tick when a policy file exists) and swarm policy check KIND --facts JSON can decide this rule, that the facts factsOf builds for a hand-build request include the file list, the git operations and the branch, and that the autopilot tick approves such a request within one pass. Policy stays inert until the owner runs swarm policy init (unchanged) and the new rule is listed by swarm policy show. Add it to docs/policy.md. Tests in tests/policy-commit-window.test.mjs (hermetic: temp project, injected clock, no ambient environment): a commit window for docs/scope/build-plan.md, coordination/manifests/x.json and .swarm/project/tickets.json on branch feat/x is auto-approved and logged with the rule id and expiry; one source file mixed in makes it owner-only; a test file, a workflow file and package.json are owner-only; a window for main, master, release/1.2, HEAD, origin/main and a missing branch is owner-only; git ops with force, delete or merge are owner-only; path tricks (docs/scope/../../tools/x.mjs, an absolute path, a symlinked dir) are owner-only; minutes above 120 are capped to 120; a missing or non-boolean fact is owner-only; the log record is written before the approval is applied and a log failure leaves the request for the owner; with no policy file nothing is auto-approved; swarm policy show lists the rule. Keep every existing test passing (the existing policy and handbuild tests). No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only policy and hand-build files and their tests change.
